**Yes, but not by Sarah. At 15%, the discount has to be approved by the VP of Sales, Michael Torres.**

Northstar Pricing Policy 2026 (in effect 2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31, so it covers 2026-09-23) sets these approval levels:

| Discount | Who approves |
|---|---|
| Up to and including 10% | Enterprise Account Executive |
| Over 10%, up to and including 20% | VP Sales |
| Over 20% | Chief Revenue Officer |

- **Sarah Chen** is an Enterprise Account Executive, so she can only approve discounts up to 10%. She can't sign off on 15% herself.
- **15%** is in the VP Sales band, so the CRO doesn't need to be involved.
- **Michael Torres** is the VP Sales. The current records show Sarah reporting to him from 2026-09-01, so he's her direct manager and the right approver on 2026-09-23.

- The knowledge base has an entry for DR-9001 but almost nothing linked to it. - For context, the NS-500 Industrial Controller lists at $250,000, so 15% would be about $37,500 per unit. That assumes this is the same product.
